title: The Junior Associate
logline: Arthur Hobbs leaves Marshall in charge of Tugboat for the weekend, with a two-hundred-page binder, hourly phone check-ins and one sacred rule: Tugboat must never find out he's a dog. Marshall takes him to the dog run anyway, and the gang spends thirty-six hours faking barks down the phone and trying to turn a schnauzer back into a lawyer, while Brad Morris angles for the gig.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Uncle Marshall's boss left him in charge of the thing he loved most in the world: his dog, Tugboat. Tugboat had worked at that law firm for nine years. He had no idea he was a dog.

scenes.summary: Marshall's law firm, Friday. Brad wants the Tugboat gig because the last sitter made partner. Arthur picks Marshall, whispers that Tugboat believes he's a junior associate, hands over the binder and sets the hourly one-bark check-in. Button: the binder's last tab already fires Marshall, laminated.

beats.line: Marshall's law firm. Friday, four fifty-nine p.m.
Marsh. Hobbs is going to Vermont for the weekend. Somebody's getting the Tug.
The Tug?
Tugboat. His dog. Last guy who dog-sat him made partner in six weeks. Fennimore.
Fennimore made partner? Fennimore eats lunch in the supply closet.
Partners can eat wherever they want, bro.
Eriksen!
Sir! I wasn't gossiping. I was billing. Out loud.
You're watching Tugboat this weekend. I leave for Vermont in four minutes.
Sir, with respect, I'm amazing with dogs. I take my corgi to brunch every—
Lower your voice. He's in my office.
Sir, does Tugboat not know that he's a...
Tugboat believes he is a junior associate at this firm. Nobody is taking that from him.
His binder. Two hundred pages, tabbed by the hour. He eats at the conference table. No mirrors. He's not ready.
And never say the word walk. We call it a site visit.
What does he do on a site visit?
He bills it.
I'll call every hour on the hour. You hold the phone to him. One bark means all is well.
And two barks?
Two barks means he wants to discuss his bonus. Do not engage.
Sir, I'm totes free this weekend. I run dog agility. I'm basically a dog lawyer.
Morris, last time you watched him, he came home expecting mimosas.
He loved those mimosas.
Eriksen, you're the only man in this office he's never bitten.
He's bitten me four times. Each time, I gave him a raise.
Sir, I won't let you down. He'll be the happiest junior associate in New York.
He doesn't need to be happy, Eriksen. He needs to be billable.
Brad, the last tab in here says, in case Tugboat finds out.
What's it say?
Eriksen, you're fired. My name's already filled in.
It's laminated.

scenes.summary: Saturday. Marshall confesses he took Tugboat to the dog run, where Tugboat met a golden retriever and found out. The three o'clock check-in: Tugboat won't bark, so Marshall barks. The gang pitches terrible fixes. Brad turns up with brunch, saw everything at the dog run, and offers a 'favor' that's a takeover. Button: Barney takes the four o'clock bark.

beats.line: By Saturday afternoon, Marshall had followed that binder for twenty-two straight hours.
Guys. Whatever happens, nobody say the word dog.
Why can't we say dog?
Because he can hear you, Ted!
Marshall. What did you do?
I took him to the dog run.
That's where dogs go.
He was at the window all morning, Robin. Watching the park. Little tail going.
I grew up on a farm, Lily. Our dogs ran ten miles a day. One of them made it to Iowa.
Five minutes, I said. Then he saw a golden retriever. They stared at each other like two guys finding out they're twins.
And then he sniffed her butt, Ted! Like some kind of dog!
He ate a sock, he barked at the radiator, and now he's asleep on our bed.
On our bed? He's a junior associate! That is so inappropriate!
Saturday, a park, sniffing strangers, passing out in someone else's bed? That dog isn't confused. That dog is me.
Three o'clock. It's Arthur. He wants his bark.
Tugboat. Buddy. One bark. Like a closing argument.
He's licking himself.
Marshall, do something!
Woof.
Yes, sir. All is well. Congested? Yes, sir. He's wearing his scarf.
Marshall, that's the most dignified bark I've ever heard.
Please. That was a junior associate bark. I bark like a senior partner.
Arthur's back Monday. I have forty-two hours to convince that dog he's a lawyer.
Dad, this might be your best story ever. You're not even in it.
I'm in it, Penny. I'm about to save the day.
Easy. My ninety-minute lecture on the load-bearing wall. Nothing makes you feel more like a professional.
Ted, a student fainted during that lecture.
From the beauty, Robin.
Nobody in a suit ever felt like an animal. I'm suiting him up. I've had a schnauzer-sized suit since 2009.
Why?
Lily. A man should be ready.
Amateurs. Every September I get twenty kids who think they're dinosaurs. By Halloween, they're people. Circle time.
And if circle time doesn't work?
Then it's my other kind of time.
Or. He's a dog. Let him be a dog, and tell Arthur.
Robin. Laminated.
Fine. I'll help. But I am not barking.
Marsh! Brought brunch. Frittata, scones, and a tiny mimosa for the Tug.
Brad! Great. Tugboat's in a meeting.
At the Riverside dog run? 'Cause I saw you two there this morning.
I run agility there on Saturdays. With my corgi, Hollandaise.
Your corgi is named Hollandaise?
Her brother's named Benedict. I'm a brunch guy, Barney. I'm not gonna apologize for it.
Real talk, Marsh. I take the Tug for the rest of the weekend. We tell Hobbs I sat him. You assisted.
That's not a favor, Brad. That's a hostile takeover.
Favor, takeover. Potato, potahto.
No.
Cool. No hard feelings, bro. May the best sitter win.
Oh no. It's four o'clock.
Watch and learn.
Woof.

scenes.summary: Montage of the gang's shifts: Ted's lecture, Robin's sound-library bark, Barney's tiny suit, Lily's circle time, Ted's pedantic bark. On the roof Sunday night, every idea has backfired, Robin's terrier was a walrus, and Arthur texts that Brad tipped him off and he's coming home. Marshall resolves to tell Arthur the truth. Button: the nine o'clock call, he tries, and barks.

beats.line: So the gang took shifts. Every hour, on the hour, for thirty-six hours.
Hour three, Mister Tugboat. The flying buttress.
Sound library, track forty-seven. Distinguished terrier.
Tugboat. Suit up.
Not the pants! Those are Italian!
Circle time, Tugboat. We do not chew Uncle Ted's cowboy boots. Even when they deserve it.
Woof. Which, fun fact, sir, is an onomatopoeia.
Okay. Status report on our junior associate.
He fell asleep twelve minutes into my lecture.
Ted, he fell asleep in a lecture. That's the most human thing he's done all weekend.
The jacket fits like a dream. The pants, he ate. Honestly? Power move.
He sat through all of circle time, then ate the talking stick. Best student I've had all year.
Robin. Track forty-seven was not a terrier.
It was mislabeled.
What was it?
Walrus.
And then I panicked and texted him woof.
beats.title: Arthur Hobbs

messages.text: Why does my dog sound like a walrus.
Morris says Tugboat is having the best weekend of his life.
Coming home early. My office. 7 a.m.

beats.line: Brad.
Okay. New plan. We fake Tugboat's death.
Barney!
A fun death! Witness protection. He moves to Phoenix, becomes a dentist.
No. Guys, you didn't see him at the dog run. Forty minutes running in circles. I've never seen anybody that happy.
Except you at the State Fair.
The butter sculpture year. Yes.
I'm not putting him back in that box, Lily. Tomorrow I tell Arthur the truth.
Marshmallow, he'll fire you.
Then I'm a fired lawyer. But that dog is going to know who he is.
Nine o'clock.
Watch this.
Sir. There's something I need to tell you.
Woof.

scenes.summary: Monday, 7 a.m. Tugboat is at Arthur's desk in Barney's jacket. Brad 'only texted'. Arthur arrives and IDs each fake barker by their bark. He knew from the first call: Tugboat has never barked on the phone. Marshall confesses anyway. Arthur's tenderness: Tugboat was the first one not afraid of him, and he feared other dogs would show him he could do better. Undercut with disbarment threats; Brad gets the agility gig, not the partner track. Arthur barks once, then twice. Future Ted: Arthur's one new friend at the dog run.

beats.line: Relax. He's at Arthur's desk, in a jacket, with a stack of files. If that's not a lawyer, I don't know what is.
He's eating the files.
He's reviewing them.
Morning, Marsh! Big day!
You told him, Brad.
I didn't tell. I texted. Huge difference, legally.
Brad, I teach kindergarten. Tattletales eat lunch alone. Forever. I make sure of it.
Eriksen! Who are all these people?
Hi. Ted Mosby, architect.
Onomatopoeia.
Barney Stinson, sir. Big fan.
Four o'clock. You purred.
He noticed.
And you're the walrus.
Technically, I never barked.
Sir, how did you know it was us?
Eriksen, Tugboat has never barked on the phone. Not once in nine years.
He just breathes. Heavily. Like a man who's read the whole contract.
Then you should hear the rest, sir. I took him to the dog run. He met other dogs. He knows.
And I'm not sorry. He ran in circles for forty minutes. I've never seen a lawyer that happy.
He's wearing a blazer.
Hugo Boss. The pants didn't make it.
Nine years ago, he bit me on the courthouse steps. First living thing in a decade that wasn't afraid of me.
So I gave him a job.
I told him he was an associate because if he ever met other dogs, he'd figure out he could do better than me.
Sir, he met forty dogs. He played with every one of them. Then he sat by our door all night, waiting for you.
If anyone repeats a word of this, I will have every one of you disbarred.
Most of us aren't lawyers.
I'll find something.
Sir! About next weekend, I'd love to take the Tug—
Morris. You run agility on Saturdays?
With Hollandaise, sir.
Tugboat starts this Saturday. You'll carry the cones.
Sir, is this the partner track?
For him.
Woof.
One bark. All is well.
Woof.
Two barks?
They're discussing his bonus.
Kids, Arthur took Tugboat to the dog run every Saturday after that. Tugboat made dozens of friends.
Arthur made exactly one. The golden retriever. He still insists she's in mergers and acquisitions.
